experiments.sample: Five volunteers with real Windows workflows, including three clean installation environments
experiments.hypothesis: A coherent portable profile with help and reversible install is valuable beyond free colors.
experiments.stop: Security/reversibility failure, no qualified demand, or repeated personal support need.
experiments.success: Proposed acceptance: three independent installs work without manual help, existing profile changes survive, and stated price choices are recorded. These criteria have not been tested.
experiments.budget: Set a bounded project budget before running the experiment. Paid conversion, receipt and refund tests require a separate released offer.

experiments.sample: Five founders in one specific niche; three independent customer-account deployments
experiments.hypothesis: A complete working offer site and agent workflow provides more value than decorative pages.
experiments.stop: Deploy requires creator credentials, generic buyer story, or no demonstrated preference.
experiments.success: Proposed acceptance: three independent customer-account deployments, working CTAs and qualified stated intent with price choices. These criteria have not been tested.
experiments.budget: Set a bounded project budget before running the experiment. Paid conversion, receipt and refund tests require a separate released offer.

experiments.sample: Three buyer-owned agent environments using one narrowly bounded workflow
experiments.hypothesis: Tested fixtures and approval boundaries make a BYOK workflow useful without founder support.
experiments.stop: Unreliable outcome, buyer cannot reproduce setup, or unsafe tool behavior.
experiments.success: Proposed acceptance: tasks complete with traceable evidence, measured run cost and no unauthorized actions; stated price choices are recorded. These criteria have not been tested.
experiments.budget: Set a bounded project budget before running the experiment. Paid conversion, receipt and refund tests require a separate released offer.

architecture.name: Define the job
architecture.behavior: Specify the buyer task, supported devices, acceptance criteria and stop condition.

architecture.name: Research the route
architecture.behavior: Keep URL, retrieval date, period, unit, contract scope and uncertainty with each claim.

architecture.name: Package the outcome
architecture.behavior: Deliver compatibility checks, fixture data, installation, permission boundaries, rollback and a license.

architecture.name: Verify independently
architecture.behavior: Test behavior, accessibility, security and economics on the exact candidate. Record failures and intervention.

architecture.name: Learn from use
architecture.behavior: Separate stated intent from paid receipts and refunds. Update decisions from observed buyer outcomes.
